priorStories.headline: France says 410,000 joined nationwide protests
priorStories.body:
France’s Interior Ministry estimated that 410,000 people joined demonstrations across the country; organizers put the turnout at nearly 800,000.

Clashes broke out as protests ended in Paris, Marseille and several other cities. Police used tear gas and water cannons, and the interior minister said nearly 1,000 people were arrested. Two people were seriously injured, while some businesses were vandalized or looted.

priorStories.headline: New York archdiocese agrees to $800 million settlement
priorStories.body:
The Archdiocese of New York and lawyers for about 1,300 people who alleged sexual abuse by clergy or other church personnel reached an $800 million settlement agreement.

The agreement still requires signatures, which are scheduled for the week of November 6. Its terms also call for the release of documents concerning alleged offenders.

priorStories.headline: Houthis fire missiles toward Saudi Arabia and Aden
priorStories.body:
The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed ballistic missiles heading toward Yanbu and Taif as Yemen’s Houthi movement claimed a wider attack on Saudi airports, oil facilities and other infrastructure. Saudi authorities had not confirmed that the claimed targets were hit.

Yemen’s internationally recognized government separately said three Houthi missiles struck coast guard sites in Aden. No casualties were immediately reported.

priorStories.headline: Typhoon Champi injures 527 people in Taiwan
priorStories.body:
Taiwan’s emergency operations center said Typhoon Champi left one person dead and 527 injured. Most injuries were linked to falling trees, power cables and billboards, as well as damaged water pipes.

The weather agency later downgraded Champi to a tropical storm and lifted its land warning.

candidates.summary: A bus collided with a truck on the Nairobi-Mombasa highway in Makueni County on Sunday morning, killing at least 22 people, police said. Several others were injured, and the county commissioner said the death toll could rise. Authorities had not determined the cause of the crash.
candidates.title: Kenya bus crash kills at least 22 people

candidates.summary: Saudi Arabia's military said air defenses intercepted Houthi missiles and drones directed toward Riyadh and southern parts of the country early Sunday. King Khalid International Airport also reopened terminals for domestic and international flights after earlier Houthi attacks had disrupted operations.
candidates.title: Saudi Arabia reports new Houthi attacks as Riyadh airport reopens

candidates.summary: The Israeli military announced restrictions barring Palestinian laborers from jobs in Israeli settlements and closed several West Bank crossings as it continued an operation launched after two Israeli soldiers were killed in Hebron on Friday.
candidates.title: Israel imposes new West Bank restrictions during military operation

candidates.summary: Voting began in Serbia's snap parliamentary election, with long lines reported outside polling stations. About 6.4 million voters were eligible to choose among 18 lists competing for the 250-seat National Assembly, in a close contest between Aleksandar Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party and the student-backed Students' List.
candidates.title: Serbia votes in closely contested parliamentary election

candidates.summary: Bulgarians began voting to elect a president from a record field of 27 candidates. Incumbent President Iliana Yotova and former caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov were regarded as the leading contenders, with a runoff considered likely because the winner must secure a majority and turnout must exceed 50%.
candidates.title: Bulgaria holds presidential election

candidates.summary: Brazilians began voting in a presidential runoff between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro finished more than 2.2 million votes ahead of Lula in the first round, but neither secured a majority. Polls opened at 8 a.m. Brasília time and were scheduled to close at 5 p.m.
candidates.title: Brazil votes in presidential runoff

candidates.summary: Ukrainian officials disputed Elon Musk's assertion that Ukraine's military violated Starlink's terms by using the civilian satellite service for offensive drone strikes. Presidential defense technology adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said longstanding restrictions made that use impossible. Musk acknowledged Saturday that SpaceX had throttled Starlink in Ukraine; Ukrainian officials said speed restrictions affecting Starlink and the military-focused Starshield service were lifted Saturday.
candidates.title: Ukraine disputes Musk's claim over military use of Starlink
